description:
Board mover, s495, CAUSED BY s492c member 7 and legitimate: with no
MIME::Base64 the dist's t/quote.t took its `else { skip("MIME::Base64
missing", 1) }` branch, so row 12 was a SKIP.  The shim makes
`eval { require MIME::Base64 }` succeed, the row RUNS, and it fails:

  Data-Dump-1.25-0 quote.t PASS 16/0 (base 5ce155cb) -> PARTIAL 16/1 (s492c)

PROBED (scratchpad dd.pl, `local $Data::Dump::TRY_BASE64 = 1;
dump(join("", map chr($_), 0..255))`):

  perl 5.40.3   402 chars, `do {\n  require MIME::Base64;\n  MIME::Base64::decode("AAEC...`
  PCL           525 chars, `pack("H*","000102...`   <- the NON-base64 branch

So the module loads and Data::Dump still does not choose base64.  Its rule is
in Data::Dump::_dump: with $TRY_BASE64 set and the string long enough and
mostly binary, it compares the two renderings' LENGTHS and takes the shorter.
Next step is to instrument that comparison under PCL -- the suspects are the
`length` of the base64 text, the `$TRY_BASE64` read across packages (#475's
family), and the `eval { require MIME::Base64 }` inside Data::Dump itself
succeeding but its `MIME::Base64::encode_base64` call not.

This is the s438h shape once more: a fix that makes a VALUE real exposes what
was passing on nothing.  The row is an honest failure and is NOT a regression
of the base64 shim itself (its own dist t/ is 437 of 495).
subject: Data::Dump's TRY_BASE64 branch is reachable now that MIME::Base64 loads -- and PCL still emits the pack("H*") form
